title: Route merge below the frontier (GATED): WinCount section (C) - dZeroBelowRecord ([Z-PT] => D(3e9) = 0 exactly, the B0.zeroD_of_RH pattern with the frontier; 0 is the even case of D_even) + rvmGateDischarged (the recorded exact count Nline implies the fleet's +-3 gate |Ntot - rvm3e9| <= 3 as a theorem, pure record arithmetic via pinGates); plus the S(t)-bound search record (best explicit unconditional bound at 3e9 is ~2.21 > the 1.875 needed, so the gate stays recorded data); full tree green 17450 jobs
body: FORMAL MILESTONE (no RH claim): the two hWin shrink routes are now MERGED below the frontier, closing the route story at 3e9.  MODULE:  formal/RhAttack/WinCount.lean section (C) (module now 451 lines; build green; full tree re-verified at 17450 jobs, 0 errors; 0 sorry).  TWO THEOREMS:  (1) dZeroBelowRecord (q : ZeroSet) (hPT : allOnLineUpTo q tPT) (ht : 0 < tdata) : D q tdata ht = 0 - for ANY zero set consistent with the cited frontier [Z-PT], the off-line excess at the record height 3e9 (= 3,000,000,000 < tPT = 30,610,046,000) is EXACTLY ZERO.  The proof is the B0.zeroD_of_RH pattern verbatim (empty-filter argument on the slice, Finset.filter_false_of_mem), with the RH hypothesis replaced by the frontier applied on (0, tPT] - every zero with 0 < Im <= 3e9 sits on the line, so the off-line slice is empty.  This is STRICTLY SHARPER than the record shadow's offExcessBound (D <= n - 1 under the +-n strip gate; at the record's tolerance n = 3, D <= 2): it replaces a gate-tolerated bound by an exact zero, and consistency is built in: 0 is the even case of D_even (no parity conflict between the two routes).  (2) rvmGateDischarged (q : ZeroSet) (ht0 : 0 < tdata) (hcount : Ntot q tdata ht0 = Nline) : abs ((Ntot q tdata ht0 : ℝ) - (rvm3e9 : ℝ)) <= 3 - for a zero set whose exact count at 3e9 matches the pinned record count Nline = 9064192826 (the ACTUAL set has exactly this recorded data), the fleet's recorded +-3 RVM finish gate holds as a THEOREM: the arithmetic is pure record content (pinGates norms Nline - rvm3e9 = 21/50 and |21/50| = 0.42 <= 3); the frontier is deliberately absent from the hypothesis list (it is not used in the arithmetic).  THE MERGE:  below tPT the two routes carry each other's load - [Z-PT] (route A, cited classical) gives D = 0, and the pinned count (route B, recorded data) re-derives the +-3 gate that offExcessBound consumes as a hypothesis.  For the actual zero set both inputs are available, so the 3e9 record shadow is fully accounted for: D(3e9) = 0 (not merely <= 2), and the +-3 gate is a theorem rather than an input.  SEARCH RECORD (the lever that did NOT land):  a fully CITED RVM error bound |S(t)| <= c at 3e9 would have made the +-3 gate cited rather than recorded (the exact RVM formula differs from the record's rvm(t) = (t/2 pi) ln(t/2 pi) - t/2 pi + 7/8 by S(t) - 5/8 - (1/8) ln(1 - t^-2), so forcing |N - rvm| <= 3 needs |S(3e9)| <= 3 - 5/8 = 1.875).  Doc-first search of explicit unconditional S(t) bounds found:  Trudgian, 'A modest improvement on the function S(T)' (arXiv:1010.4596; Math. Comp. 78 (2009) 1-18): |S(T)| <= 0.1013 log T for large T - at 3e9 this is 0.1013 * 21.82 = 2.21, ABOVE the 1.875 needed;  Trudgian II (arXiv:1208.5846): |S(T)| <= 0.111 log T + 0.275 log log T + 2.450 for all T >= e - 5.89 at 3e9;  Fujii-type explicit bounds (0.015338 log T + 4.4943) - 4.83 at 3e9;  the RH-conditional (1/8 pi) log T ~ 0.87 is unusable (circular).  Conclusion: no available explicit unconditional bound certifies the +-3 gate from the RVM formula alone; the gate remains RECORDED DATA (as the fleet actually ran it at 3e9, and as the record shadow states it), and the route merge above is the clean closure of the 3e9 story.  CARDS:  99 cards / 886 body lines (WinCount card extended with section (C) + the endpoint-consumer note from discovery 0107; RHEnd card from 0107); _MAP.md carries the 'WinCount (C) (the ROUTE MERGE below the frontier)' block; PATHWAY-TO-A-SOLUTION.md carries the merge paragraph with the search record after the Part B3 paragraph.  NEXT LEVER candidates:  (a) B7F consumer wiring (recon needed: the card's 'walk (B1) / law-territory (B5)' names predate the current module layout - the current B5 is the detector deviation-ratio piece; identify the actual consumer before implementing);  (b) the hs1 height-uniformity measured piece (P1.1e / 25x margin regime - data run then pinning; the largest remaining measured face at the endpoint);  (c) the 3e10 frontier (tPT = 3.06e10) already exceeds the 3e9 H1 run - a future H1 run toward 3e10 would extend the measured zero walk toward the frontier and shrink what [Z-PT] has to cite.
